title: A Lantern for the Orchard
premise: In the winter of 1853, in the river town of Vellamont, apprentice mapmaker Ines Halloran inherits the unfinished atlas of his dead master, Aldous Vane — an atlas that quietly records the orchard villages the Crown intends to flood for a canal, villages whose land titles the government has falsified. When the season's last bridge closes, Ines is trapped among the very people Vane documented, including the orchard keeper Maren and her found family of displaced laborers, who slowly become his own. As the victors' surveyors arrive to write the official history, Ines must choose between the safe anonymity his master urged and putting the true atlas on the record — knowing it will cost him his post, perhaps his freedom. He smuggles the atlas out in pieces, carried by those who owe the orchards their memories, and the truth survives in many hands even as the waters rise.
about_author: Ulyana Coldharbour is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing disputed land surveys in municipal basements. She writes historical fiction about the documents that outlive the people who risked everything to keep them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. He catalogues Aldous Vane's effects the morning after the funeral, hiding the unfinished atlas beneath floorboards when the guild steward comes to inventory the workshop. Emotional beat: grief tangled with the first flicker of defiance — he has already decided not to hand everything over.

chapters.title: Ink and Inheritance
chapters.summary: Ines studies Vane's marginalia and realizes the atlas documents the orchard villages' true boundaries, contradicting the Crown's canal survey. Flashbacks establish Vane as a distant, exacting mentor. Emotional beat: dawning understanding that the atlas was a deliberate act, and that Ines was chosen to finish it.

chapters.title: Orders Come Down
chapters.summary: The guild receives official notice: all Vane materials are Crown property, to be surrendered before the survey commission arrives in spring. The steward pressures Ines to comply. Emotional beat: fear — Ines, an orphan apprentice with no standing, sees how easily he can be erased.

chapters.title: The Last Crossing
chapters.summary: Ines plans to slip across the bridge with the atlas before winter closes the road, but ice and a collapsed span strand the town. POV shifts to Maren, the orchard keeper, watching the bridge fail from the far bank of her own life. Emotional beat: the trap closes; staying is no longer a choice.

chapters.title: A Room Above the Cooper's
chapters.summary: Ines takes lodgings in the working quarter, out of the guild's reach, and meets the displaced laborers Maren shelters. He says nothing about the atlas. Emotional beat: the discomfort of a man trained to be invisible suddenly surrounded by people who notice him.

chapters.title: Maren's Ledger
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She keeps her own record — names, harvests, debts owed to orchard families — and recognizes a fellow keeper of accounts in Ines. She asks what he carries. He lies. Emotional beat: the first crack in his secrecy, and the first pull of belonging.

chapters.title: What the Surveyors Burn
chapters.summary: A Crown advance rider arrives early, burning 'redundant' parish records at the chapel. Ines watches deeds turn to ash — the very documents Vane's atlas was drawn from. Emotional beat: horror sharpening into urgency; the official history is already being written.

chapters.title: The Orchard in Winter
chapters.summary: Ines walks the frostbound orchards with Maren's adopted son Teodor, a boy who knows every tree by name. Ines sketches, telling himself it's practice. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness — the land stops being data and becomes a place.

chapters.title: Guild of One
chapters.summary: The guild steward, half-sympathetic, warns Ines that the commission's historian, Corvus Lyle, is already asking about Vane's 'missing' folios. Ines realizes hiding is a countdown, not a refuge. Emotional beat: paranoia; every knock at the door could be the end.

chapters.title: The Marginal Hand
chapters.summary: Ines deciphers Vane's cipher in the atlas margins — instructions for splitting the atlas into portable parts, each to be carried by a different hand. Emotional beat: awe and dread; his master planned for exactly this, and never trusted one person alone.

chapters.title: Bread and Boundaries
chapters.summary: Maren's household dinner; Ines is asked, plainly, whose side he's on. He deflects, and Teodor calls him a coward — gently. Emotional beat: shame; loyalty is being demanded before he understands what he owes.

chapters.title: Corvus Lyle Arrives
chapters.summary: Lyle's POV. The victors' historian reaches the far bank, blocked by the closed bridge, and begins interviewing by letter — charming, meticulous, ruthless. He writes that Vane was 'a talented eccentric.' Emotional beat: cold dread; Lyle is already rewriting the dead man.

chapters.title: The First Split
chapters.summary: Ines copies the atlas's western sheets and entrusts them to Maren, confessing everything at last. She accepts the pages without ceremony. Emotional beat: relief and terror — the secret is shared, which means it can be betrayed.

chapters.title: A Debt in the Parish Book
chapters.summary: POV of Father Anselm, who hid orchard deeds during the last seizure and paid for it with his post. He offers Ines the parish's hidden strongbox of original documents. Emotional beat: the weight of inherited courage — others have bled for this record before.

chapters.title: The Steward's Price
chapters.summary: The guild steward offers Ines restoration of his post and Vane's reputation if he surrenders the atlas 'for safekeeping.' Ines sees the trap: safekeeping means the fire. Emotional beat: temptation — a legitimate life, offered in exchange for silence.

chapters.title: Ice on the Canal Route
chapters.summary: Ines and Teodor scout the frozen canal bed — the future flood line — and find the surveyors' stakes already driven into orchard soil. Teodor pulls one up. Emotional beat: quiet fury made physical; the erasure has already begun in the ground.

chapters.title: Letters to a Stranger
chapters.summary: Lyle corresponds with Ines directly, flattering him as Vane's true heir, fishing for the atlas's location. Ines answers with careful half-truths. Emotional beat: a duel in ink; Ines discovers he can lie well, and hates how much he enjoys it.

chapters.title: The Night the Cooper Sang
chapters.summary: A found-family chapter: songs, stories, the household's rituals of memory — each laborer recites where they were born and who they lost. Ines is asked again, and this time he answers with his own true story. Emotional beat: belonging, finally, and the cost of it — he now has something to lose.

chapters.title: Betrayal in Small Print
chapters.summary: The steward, pressed by Lyle, reveals that Ines received Vane's papers. Lyle petitions to have the bridge 'reopened for official traffic' — meaning his men, and no one else. Emotional beat: the net tightening; the truth is now contraband.

chapters.title: Maren's Choice
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She must decide whether the household shelters the atlas openly — making them all accomplices — or sends Ines away to protect them. She chooses to stand. Emotional beat: loyalty declared; the found family formally becomes a conspiracy of memory.

chapters.title: The Second Split
chapters.summary: The atlas is divided: maps to the cooper, cipher keys to Father Anselm, the land-title proofs to Maren. Ines keeps only the master index, sewn into his coat. Emotional beat: sacrificial relief — the truth no longer lives or dies with one man.

chapters.title: What Lyle Offers
chapters.summary: Lyle crosses the ice with an escort and confronts Ines face to face: immunity, employment on the official history, a name in the record — if the atlas is 'corrected' to match the Crown survey. Emotional beat: the devil's arithmetic; Ines understands Lyle sincerely believes he is saving history from chaos.

chapters.title: The Master's Last Page
chapters.summary: Ines finds Vane's final, unfinished page: a confession that Vane falsified nothing but once did, long ago, and built the atlas as penance. Emotional beat: complicated grief — his master was both coward and martyr, and Ines must be braver.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: Lyle's men, 'recovering Crown property,' ransack the guildhouse and the cooper's shop. The hidden sheets survive by hours. A laborer, Piet, is arrested as a warning. Emotional beat: fear becomes anger; the abstract stakes now have a face behind bars.

chapters.title: Testimony of the Orchard
chapters.summary: The household gathers testimony — sworn statements from orchard families, dictated to Ines in the chapel cellar. Father Anselm marries the record to the old deeds. Emotional beat: solemn power; for one night, the town becomes its own historian.

chapters.title: Piet in the Lockup
chapters.summary: Ines visits Piet and offers to trade himself. Piet refuses: 'You're the pen. We're the ink.' Emotional beat: Ines grasps his role — not the hero, the instrument — and accepts it without grandiosity.

chapters.title: The Steward Repents
chapters.summary: The guild steward, confronted with Vane's confession page, defects — he unlocks the guild archive and shows Ines the Crown's forged survey plates. Emotional beat: an enemy becomes an ally; even institutions contain doubters.

chapters.title: Forged Lines
chapters.summary: Ines, a trained mapmaker, proves the forgery — the survey's river bends are geometrically impossible. He drafts a technical refutation that even Lyle's own surveyors would have to concede. Emotional beat: competence as resistance; the pen sharpened to a blade.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: The ice begins to break; the bridge will open within weeks, and with it Lyle's commission, the canal crews, the flood. The household races to finish copying the atlas. Emotional beat: hope and doom in the same sound of cracking ice.

chapters.title: The Courier Plan
chapters.summary: The copies will leave with spring's first travelers — pilgrims, drovers, a wedding party — each carrying pages, none knowing the whole. Maren's POV as she assigns the routes. Emotional beat: trust radicalized; the truth distributed like seed.

chapters.title: Lyle's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Lyle writes one final letter: not a threat but a warning — the canal is approved, the flood is certain, and only Ines's surrender can buy Piet's release and the town's mercy. Emotional beat: despair's genuine logic; the offer is almost kind, which makes it worse.

chapters.title: The Long Night of Copying
chapters.summary: The household copies the atlas by lantern light — the orchard lanterns, the book's namesake — while Ines drafts the master refutation. Teodor, too young for the risk, is entrusted with the single most important page. Emotional beat: exhausted communion; the found family at its most unified.

chapters.title: Surrender at the Guildhall
chapters.summary: Ines walks into the guildhall and gives Lyle the atlas — the original, as demanded — while the copies are already on the road. Lyle, triumphant, begins to 'correct' it. Emotional beat: calculated sacrifice dressed as defeat; Ines must look broken and isn't.

chapters.title: The Bridge Opens
chapters.summary: The bridge reopens; the commission crosses in triumph. Ines is dismissed from the guild, formally disgraced. Emotional beat: the hollow after surrender — he has lost everything visible and must believe in what's invisible.

chapters.title: What the Pages Carried
chapters.summary: POVs of the couriers, one by one: the drover, the pilgrim, the bride — each page arriving at a priory, a solicitor, a newspaper office in the capital. Emotional beat: scattered hope becoming momentum; the truth is now unownable.

chapters.title: The Refutation Published
chapters.summary: A capital gazette prints the geometric refutation alongside orchard testimony. Lyle's surveyors privately concede the forgery; the commission fractures. Piet is quietly released. Emotional beat: vindication, muted — the canal may still come, but the lie is dead.

chapters.title: Lyle's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Lyle's POV. Facing inquiry, he burns the 'corrected' atlas rather than let it stand as his work — an act Ines interprets, generously, as Lyle's own penance. Emotional beat: the enemy's humanity; history's victors are also its prisoners.

chapters.title: The Waters Rise
chapters.summary: The canal proceeds; the orchard floods as the law requires. The household stands on the ridge and watches the water take the trees. Maren reads names aloud from her ledger. Emotional beat: grief without defeat — the land is lost, the record is not.

chapters.title: A Lantern for the Orchard
chapters.summary: Ines, restored by the gazette's vindication but refusing his old post, founds a small archive above the cooper's shop — the town's own record, kept by its own people. He hangs a lantern in the window for the drowned orchard. Emotional beat: quiet resolve; memory institutionalized as care.

chapters.title: The Atlas That Remained
chapters.summary: Years later, an elderly Ines receives a letter: a priory has reunited the scattered pages, and the true atlas will be published with every courier's name in the front matter. Teodor, now a surveyor of honest maps, stands beside him. Emotional beat: fulfillment — the world was measured in what could be carried, and it was enough.
